title: 12 Object detection
overview:
This is the opening page of **chapter 12, Object detection**. The "This chapter covers" box lists four topics:

- understanding the object detection problem,
- two-stage and single-stage object detectors,
- training a simple single-stage detector from scratch,
- using a pretrained object detector.

The opening paragraph defines the task: object detection is "all about drawing boxes (called *bounding boxes*) around objects of interest in a picture" (see Figure 12.1, printed on p.354). Detection tells you **which** objects are present and **where** they are. Three common applications follow:

- **Counting**: how many instances of an object are in an image;
- **Tracking**: following how objects move in a scene by running detection on every frame of a movie;
- **Cropping**: locating the region containing an object of interest so that a higher-resolution patch can be sent to a classifier or an Optical Character Recognition (OCR) model.

How to use this page: treat it as a map. According to the chapter outline, section 12.1 (p.354) contrasts two-stage R-CNN detectors with single-stage detectors, 12.2 (p.356) trains a YOLO model from scratch on COCO, and 12.3 (p.370) uses a pretrained RetinaNet. The page connects directly to chapter 11: the box prompts used with SAM on p.351-352 are exactly the kind of bounding box a detector outputs, and p.354 will argue that segmentation is a strict superset of detection but much costlier to run and to label.
